raw_response:
I farm the way I always have: I look at what worked last year, then I shift a little if I think the weather or price may change. My land is only 3 mu, so every bag of fertilizer costs real money, but I still would rather put a bit more than too little, because if yield falls, that hurts more than wasting some fertilizer. Here in Quzhou, wheat and maize take turns on the same land, and with well water in hand I do not dare leave the crop thirsty at the key time. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough base fertilizer in, water a few times, and keep an eye on weeds and aphids. For maize after wheat, I will still use hybrid seed like most people do now, because I have seen it give fuller ears than old seed. I will give maize a good first fertilizer and one topdressing, water it when it needs it, and spray if worms or leaf disease show up. I do not chase fancy ways. I do what I have seen work on fields around me, and on my small land I keep the plan steady so I can bring the crop in safely.
